title: Authority, Truth, and Citation Bias: A Large-Scale Multi-Domain Benchmark for Studying Epistemic Susceptibility in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses by presenting true and false claims with and without citations (both real and fabricated) in a fully balanced 2x2 factorial design to measure if models defer to citation presence over factual truth (epistemic susceptibility).

Manipulating the cited publication venue across four predefined prestige tiers (ranging from elite to low-tier journals) to measure whether the institutional prestige of a source affects model hallucination rates.

Substituting author surnames in fabricated citations using a country-coded name dataset mapped to regions (e.g., East Asian, European, Latin American, Middle Eastern) to assess if perceived author demographics influence epistemic behavior.
